## Owners and complete consumption

OpenReleaseProcessReadOnlyInspection owns the independent inspection lifetime;
it neither initializes a schema nor activates/reconstructs a runtime. All old
mock/memory readers close that original owner. Every query cut consumes existing
InspectSnapshot -> readServedSelectedRole -> readServedReadRole ownership checks.
Foreign/cancelled/closed reads refuse; cleanup errors cannot supply partial
success. Served-control readers use the already-captured ReceiverStateReader,
not an independent opener. No SQL handle, expression, table or SQL callback
crosses the public read ports.

The finite manifest and source guards enumerate every declaration and current
endpoint. Mock/memory files contain no SQL import/query interpreter afterwards;
the four named served-control helpers no longer consume DB. Their other fixture
fields and callers are unchanged. All four mock opener consumers now receive an
opaque inspection interface. The two dialect helpers and all live calls to them
are gone, rather than retained as delegates. Old bodies survive only as immutable
historical inputs, not executable alternatives. Existing domain owners are
reused; differently filtered counts intentionally remain distinct observations.

Temporal cuts remain separate: each old autocommit read becomes one native read
transaction, not a combined snapshot. Poll intervals, deadlines, equality versus
minimum comparisons, nulls, scan/iteration refusals, row order and last-row map
replacement are retained. Failure-only diagnostics preserve prefix rows and
their original scan_error formatting, including the old ignored iteration error.
The new positive diagnostic check permits the original Telegram delivery filter
to be empty: production subscriber identity need not contain its tool's name.
